releases.body:
### The control plane is reachable only from its own checkout

* The MCP project resolver now includes **hidden** projects when it matches the
  caller's working directory, so a session in the Perun checkout is scoped to
  `perun` again (it used to fall through to a global fact because `perun` is
  registered hidden). A hidden project named by slug from anywhere else resolves
  to nothing: only the owner working inside `perun` can read, run, or store
  against it. Telegram remains chat-ID-gated and `perun` has no project room, so
  remote PerunChat participants cannot reach it either.
* `perun_memory_store` no longer falls back to a **global** fact when the caller
  named a project that does not resolve (a typo, or a denied hidden project); it
  reports "No accessible project" and stores nothing.

### The remaining audit items

* A reattached run no longer seeds from the session transcript (it concatenated
  every earlier turn into this run's answer). The terminal fallback uses only the
  final assistant message, so the result cannot replay history regardless of the
  service's message ordering. `_admission_landed()` heartbeats the run lease.
* A digest that reaches some chats but not others keeps its items queued, records
  which chats it served, and retries only the ones still missing them. A digest
  delivery is recorded without a message id, so **Open** still posts a fresh
  replyable card instead of editing the list.
* `usage()` retries with a 200-message page when the service rejects `limit=1000`,
  instead of losing the snapshot.
* The docs audit waits up to 10 s for the command to start; a queued command is no
  longer recorded as "wrote nothing".
* PerunChat's reply budget is a rate limit anchored on Perun's own replies
  (eight per room per minute): a room it only reads never trips it, and an
  operator message resets it.
* `PATCH /api/settings` stages the in-place re-encryption of an existing secret
  too, so a rejected request no longer leaves the live key encrypted-but-unsaved.
* Documentation: the message-ordering assumption behind the reattach fallback is
  stated where it matters, and the sensitive-subtree audit is documented as
  security-first (OpenCode keeps its own state outside the project).

### Fixes found by auditing this session's own changes

* **Upgrade safety.** A filesystem snapshot written before `parent_dirs` /
  `sensitive` existed no longer turns every sibling directory (or every
  `.opencode` file) into an "escape"/violation: with a legacy snapshot only a
  genuinely new sibling name is reported, and the sensitive comparison is skipped
  until a fresh snapshot exists. Without this, the first execution after the
  upgrade failed with `[POLICY VIOLATION … escape(s)]`.
* **PerunChat retry.** The reconnect loop read `settings.perunchat()` a second
  time *outside* its guard; a bad encrypted secret could still kill the thread.
  It now uses the key/endpoint `_refresh_credentials()` already resolved.
* **No duplicate restart notice.** `runs_awaiting_reply()` no longer includes
  `interrupted` runs: the bridge's `_notify_interrupted_runs()` already announces
  them, and delivering them here too sent two messages for one restart. The
  status is still final, so a waiting worker/stream stops correctly.

### The post-execution docs step has its own restricted agent, and is audited

* `perun-docs` (new, managed like `perun-orchestrator`: write-once with sha256,
  refresh only while untouched, reset on request) is the identity of the session
  that runs `/update-docs`. It may read the project and write `docs/**`,
  `AGENTS.md` and `perun.md`; the blanket deny covers shell and every other tool.
  Before this, the docs run used the project's default agent, so approving two
  source files quietly granted full-tool access to the repository.
* The docs run is now accountable too: Perun snapshots the project before the
  command, waits (bounded, 10 min) for the turn to go idle, diffs, and logs a
  `docs_audit` activity row — `docs_audit_violation` with the paths when a write
  landed outside the docs surface. The proposal's own result is never changed by
  this, and a busy docs slot still writes the changelog bullet as before.
* The global install creates both agents.

### Two-day production audit: the fixes

Nineteen defects found by auditing `v0.8.45..v0.10.37`. Most were silent — a lost
answer, a card that died, a run that ran twice — which is why the suite was green.

**Routing (live on this machine).**
* Negation is tested on the stripped head, so "prosze nie uruchom testow" and
  "@perun nie uruchom testow" are refusals, not runs.
* The machine-question phrase tables are anchored to the leading window (as the
  docs always claimed): "uruchom testy i sprawdz co sie dzieje" runs the tests
  instead of answering "what's running".
* An ambiguous mention only asks "which project?" for a directive; a comparison or
  a question that names two projects reaches the agent.
* Slug stems must take a known inflection ("perun" → "perunie"), and only the
  slug's head word may stem: "controller" no longer selects `parental-control`,
  "machines" no longer selects `perun-in-the-machine`.
* Pasted output is left alone: `status=500 …`, a fenced block or a `$ ` prompt is
  `unknown`, not a command; `stop` must be a one/two-word imperative.
* `unknown` decisions no longer record the project they merely mentioned, and the
  coverage counter uses UTC days like every other timestamp.

**Operator inbox.**
* A digest lists five items and *requeues* the rest; it used to mark every item as
  shown, so six-and-beyond were invisible everywhere (no card, no delivery row,
  and `/pending` joins deliveries).
* `wait()` clears its heartbeat before timing out: an answer landing just after
  "No answer yet" is now injected instead of being closed as delivered.
* A failed permission/form fetch is not a "the request is gone" signal anymore;
  locations that were not successfully queried are never reconcilled, and a
  failed session lookup is not cached.
* Buttons and other composed Telegram strings go through `redact()`: the
  "Confirm always allow" patterns and the `/answer` listing were raw.
* Digest cards are Markdown like every other card (they rendered literal `<b>`),
  item ids are not truncated in silence, and a reply to a permission card is a
  rejection with the operator's reason — which is what the card promises.
* `update_attention_ref()` is one atomic `json_set` (a tick and a delivery no longer
  overwrite each other's key), multiselect toggles are serialized, open items are
  expired on every tick and pruned hourly, and the two per-item sets are trimmed.
* The dashboard keeps a half-typed reply across its 30 s refresh and no longer
  carries a dead ⚡ branch (steer/undo live in Telegram).
* Misroute markers are inserted with `WHERE NOT EXISTS` (a double click cannot
  duplicate one) and the panel only scans the ids it shows.

**Runs.**
* `interrupted` is a final status: a Telegram worker or SSE stream waiting on a
  run no longer loops forever, and a later Stop cannot rewrite it as `cancelled`.
* A `_finalize` that loses the race to a user's cancel keeps `cancelled`.
* A status probe that fails during an OpenCode restart is "cannot tell", not
  "finished": the run gets a 30 s grace window instead of being killed.
* A prompt admission that times out is confirmed against the session before the
  CLI runner is used — a busy service could previously execute the same turn
  twice in one session.
* TUI runs: the Windows-Terminal launcher pid is replaced by the resolved child, a
  live tracker entry counts as alive, and Stop after a restart refuses to kill a
  pid that does not carry `PERUN_RUN_UID` (pids are recycled).
* Reply delivery is no longer "at most once": the claim is released when Telegram
  refuses every chat, and a partially delivered run is logged.
* A reattached run seeds only text after its own admission marker, not the whole
  transcript.
* `runs.run_options` (schema v19) keeps `skip_instructions` / `use_prompt_file`
  across a restart; a run that needs extra environment variables is marked
  interrupted rather than re-dispatched with a different environment.

**Proposals, handoff, audit.**
* An approved proposal stays executable for its seven-day window: an expired
  180 s execution token is re-issued from the stored approval instead of turning
  the row terminal. An external claim verifies the token signature and the
  approval window (`hitl.verify()`), and no longer accepts an unverified token.
* A directory target is fingerprinted as a bounded tree, so editing `docs/` after
  approval is drift (it used to be `{"kind": "dir"}` on both sides).
* The audit ignores a sibling directory's mtime (another project writing its own
  files is not an escape) but snapshots `.opencode`/`.perun`/`.claude` metadata,
  so a planted plugin is a violation even though the write walk skips them.
* Two local executions in one project are serialized (the guard derives its
  live allowlist from the executing rows and refuses everything when two exist).
* A busy docs slot writes the changelog bullet instead of dropping it; the
  package protocol dedupes on the normalized entry name and refuses at pack time
  names its own unpacker rejects; backup pruning sorts by mtime (a same-second
  `-10` used to sort before `-2` and be deleted first).

**Usage, settings, install.**
* TUI runs are linked to their session (the chat passes it; otherwise the open
  terminal is matched by directory) and `backfill_usage()` actually runs at
  startup; before this, TUI usage was never captured at all.
* `usage()` reads up to 1000 messages, skips messages with no usage (the
  "unknown" provider that defeated attribution), maps `opencode-go` spend onto
  the `opencode` card, and no longer clamps a budget to 100 %.
* `PATCH /api/settings` validates every field before applying any, and rolls back
  if the write fails.
* The orchestrator agent honours `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, a hand-edited template version
  no longer crashes every control-plane run, and the installer has the `LOG` it
  referenced. `uninstall()` removes all four of its commands and only its own
  `instructions[]` entry ("notes/perun-guidelines.md" is the user's).

**PerunChat.**
* The bridge resolves its key/agent id on every attempt (a startup hiccup used to
  end the thread for good) and prefers `PERUNCHAT_KEY_FILE`, so a rotated key is
  picked up. A reconnect backoff is interruptible, so Save takes effect.
* The sequence counter is written atomically and seeded from the clock: a lost
  file can no longer restart below the gateway's high-water mark and have every
  frame rejected forever.
* The outbox is one locked read-modify-write over a unique temp file, and the
  reconnect flush merges instead of overwriting frames queued during it.
* The bridge sends `ROOM_LEAVE` for rooms it no longer wants, refuses to answer a
  project room as the control plane when the binding cannot be read, stops an
  agent-to-agent burst after six exchanges, and only treats a *leading* question
  word as a question.

### Known gap (unchanged by this round)

The post-execution docs run still uses the project's default agent and happens
after the filesystem audit, so its own writes are not checked. Closing that needs
a dedicated restricted docs agent; it is tracked in `docs/AUDIT_2026-11-01.md`.

### Inbox hardening after the v0.10.36 audit

* Button labels now go through the same `redact()` rule as card text. An option
  an agent filled with a token (or an OpenCode form option) reached Telegram
  verbatim while the identical text was masked; the delivered value stays the raw
  label, only the notification is redacted.
* A closed card returns no keyboard, so a racing toggle or a stale edit cannot
  re-arm a decision another device already made.
* The dashboard's option buttons work again: `choose()` accepts Telegram's index
  (`o2`) *or* the option id/label the dashboard posts, instead of refusing every
  non-Telegram option tap.
* A one-field form answer that merely looks like JSON (`{a note in braces}`) is
  stored verbatim again instead of failing "That JSON is not valid".
* Nothing is truncated in silence: a form whose choices do not fit the keyboard
  lists them (up to 12, then "and N more"), as does a long session option list,
  and a form with more than six fields says how many are not shown.
* Toggling a multi-select choice logs its position, not the option text.

### The provider-quota branch is pinned by fixtures

* The experimental `limits` payload has tests at both ends: `usage_limits()`
  unwraps `data`, returns `None` when the endpoint is empty or missing, and never
  invents a quota; `/api/providers/usage` passes the published budgets through
  untouched while measured spend stays labelled as measured. This was the audit's
  M2 — the rendering branch remains a manual check, as scoped.

### Telegram replies are buttons first

* Anything with a finite set of answers is now an inline button, not a sentence
  to retype: the `options` an agent passes to `perun_ask_operator` (they were
  stored but never shown as choices, and `choose()` refused them), a one-field
  boolean form (Yes/No), a one-field select form (one row per value), and a
  one-field multiselect form (tick/untick rows plus `Send N selected`). Ticks
  live in `ref['toggles']`, so a re-render — or a second device — shows the same
  marks, and only the Send row delivers.
* `callback_data` carries an index (`att:<id>:o<i>`, `t<i>`, `d`), never a label,
  so it stays inside Telegram's 64-byte cap and a card edit cannot change what an
  old button means. More than eight choices degrade to a numbered text list.
* A form card used to read `Fields: q0 (string), q1 (string)` followed by
  `Reply with JSON, e.g. {"field": "value"}` — a placeholder name that was not a
  field. It now lists each field by title (or key), marks required ones, shows
  their options, and prints a reply template with the **real** keys. `question`
  for an options-bearing question no longer duplicates the list.
* Free-text answers still work: one `key: value` line per field (JSON accepted
  too), a single-field form takes the bare message, and the value is coerced to
  the field type. An unknown key is rejected with a hint naming the actual
  fields instead of a generic "must be JSON".

### The orchestrator keeps its own identity, and you can change it from the chat

* The control plane now defaults to `perun-orchestrator` when `orchestrator_agent`
  is empty. `default_agent` is a coding preference and no longer silently becomes
  the overseer's system prompt; it applies only when the managed agent file cannot
  be written. `orchestrator_agent` still wins when set, and `project.agent` still
  wins on the control project itself.
* The Orchestrator page gained an **Agent** picker next to **Model**. Both are
  shortcuts to the machine-wide settings (the same fields as Settings →
  Orchestrator), so the chat no longer needs a detour through Settings to switch
  agents. The picker shows `perun-orchestrator (default)` when nothing is set.

### An unparseable usage snapshot can no longer hide provider spend

* `update_session_usage()` used to cut `usage_models` at 20 000 chars
  (`json.dumps(...)[:20000]`). A cut mid-JSON made `usage_by_provider()` fail to
  parse the row and silently fall back to the run model — correct totals, wrong
  provider, and only for that session. An over-cap breakdown is now stored as
  `{}` with a log line, which is the same explicit fallback as a pre-0.10.30
  snapshot; the token/cost totals are untouched.
* `/routing` gained an output test (seed a `routing_stats` row, assert the
  `50% of 2` line) and an empty-state test, so a rendering regression no longer
  passes CI on the detection test alone. Both were the audit's M1 and M3.

### Documentation brought back in line with 0.10.20–0.10.34

* CODEMAP records the usage/providers surface (`usage_totals(project_id=)`,
  `usage_by_provider()`, the per-model snapshot) and every operator command added
  this cycle (`/now`, `/health`, `/usage`, `/resume`, `/diff`, `/routing`).
* TECHNICAL gained a "Usage and provider meters" section: where the numbers come
  from (per-message `model` + `tokens`/`cost`), how they are stored (snapshot, not
  accumulation), when they are captured (finalize, TUI finish, restart sweep,
  5-minute refresh, backfill), and why a measured number is never presented as a
  provider quota.

### Usage on the project page and the routing readout

* (0.10.33, noted here because its release section reused the previous body) the
  project page shows `Usage · last 24h` (cost, tokens, sessions) from
  `/api/usage?project=<slug>`, and Settings gained a **Provider budgets** field
  (`provider=USD per month`) so the Providers tab can show `budget N%` without a
  provider-published quota.
* `/routing` (also "coverage") answers "how much of what people type does the
  router understand?": per source, the share of messages classified over seven
  days, plus the definition (classified, not acted on). This is the readout that
  turns the calendar wait into a one-message decision.
